title: Route economics chronicle: unified cost & latency chronicle per route/model/customer
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: build a single backend service (Chronicle) that produces deterministic, queryable per-route/model/customer cost and latency chronicles suitable for Console dashboards, alerting, and exports. The service must support streaming ingestion from runtime events and daily batch reconciliation to correct out-of-order events and produce stable aggregates that can be joined to traces and billing records.

Scope:
- Ingest runtime telemetry (token counts, model variant used, hardware SKU, latency spans, KV cache hits/misses, batching window id, fallback events).
- Enrich events with route metadata (route id, route config snapshot id, customer id, pricing profile) from the routing catalog service.
- Compute incremental per-route per-model per-customer metrics with a two-level approach: low-latency streaming increments for near real-time console views and a nightly reconciliation pass to create canonical chronicles for billing and audit.
- Emit time-series and fast lookup materialized views required by Console: last-24h breakdown, 7d trend, rolling SLO attainment per route/model/tenant, and per-request attribution traces.

Non-goals: full billing invoice generation (handled by billing pipeline), in-depth cost model simulation UI (handled by Optimize team).
acceptance_criteria: Chronicle service accepts runtime events and enriches them within 60s for streaming views
Nightly reconciliation produces canonical per-route/model/customer records for previous day with <0.1% divergence from raw sums after deduplication
Console APIs return route breakdowns (cost, token counts, avg latency, p95/p99) for arbitrary 1h/24h/7d windows within 300ms for top-10k routes
Attribution lineage links to runtime trace ids and production billing ids for manual audits
Backfill/migration from legacy econ ledger is available and documented with a dry-run mode
tasks: Define event schema extension and versioning strategy for runtime to emit batching_id, fallback_reason, and cache_hit boolean
Implement streaming enrichment worker that joins route metadata with a snapshot cache and falls back to async resolution
Design compact on-disk canonical record format for nightly chronicles (columnar parquet with partitioning by date/customer/route)
Implement dedupe & correction logic in reconciliation to handle late-arriving events and duplicate trace IDs
Expose read APIs: /chronicle/route/{id}/breakdown and /chronicle/customer/{id}/summary with pagination and filter by model, region, and deployment-mode
Instrument cost estimation helpers: kernel-cost lookup by hardware SKU, per-token compute multiplier, and KV-cache saving heuristics
Add end-to-end tests with synthetic traffic including fallbacks and autoscaling bursts
Create migration job to reconcile legacy econ-ledger into nightly chronicles with approval gates

2026-01-29 Priya Singh (PM): Confirmed UI needs: last-24h top 50 routes, compare by model variant, and ability to drill into trace-level charge. Added to acceptance criteria.
2026-02-02 Design review (Maya Patel): Recommended using lightweight heatmap tiles for Console to avoid expensive joins; will provide component spec in Design PR.
2026-02-05 Engineering sync: Prototype streaming enrichment worker created. Observed 20% memory overhead in snapshot cache; exploring LRU + async fetch to reduce memory footprint.

2026-02-10 Security review request: no PII expected in Chronicle records; ensure customer_id is pseudonymized in exports. Security flagged export audit and suggested allowlist. Security ticket: SEC-1142.

2026-02-11 Diego Martinez: Implemented CM sketch for token counts in streaming layer to keep windowed memory bounded. Nightly pass will compute exact counts and overwrite sketches for canonical results.
design_decisions: Hybrid ingestion: streaming increments for low-latency Console surfaces + nightly canonicalization to fix ordering and duplicates
Use deterministic attribution: assign cost at the smallest attributable unit (request) using trace_id; streaming writes are tentative and reconciled nightly
Storage format: partitioned parquet for nightly canonicals and ClickHouse for streaming, with TTL of 90 days for streaming tables
Approximate algos in streaming (Count-Min, HyperLogLog) allowed only for ephemeral views; canonical records must be exact
Enrichment cache eviction: LRU with event-driven invalidation from routing-catalog changefeed to avoid stale route pricing
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: High cardinality (route x model x customer) will blow up storage. Mitigation: add configurable sampling for low-value tenants and rollup rules that aggregate sub-routes under a parent route for Console until user requests full granularity.
Risk: Late-arriving traces cause negative corrections that confuse end-users. Mitigation: surface reconciliation status in Console and keep tentative/canonical columns with timestamps.
Risk: Cost of pipeline exceeds value. Mitigation: track pipeline infra spend vs. feature adoption and expose opt-out per-tenant; start with conservative retention and scale based on usage.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): Implement ingestion + enrichment, run in shadow mode writing to streaming tables only; Console reads continue to use legacy aggregations
Phase 2 (2 weeks): Nightly reconciliation job developed and run in dry-run comparing new canonical sums to legacy ledger; surface diffs to engineers and finance
Phase 3 (1 week): Enable read-side feature flags for Console to fetch from Chronicle for a subset of beta customers
Phase 4 (2 weeks): Full rollout and deprecation of legacy aggregator after 7 days of parity and sign-off from Finance
metrics_to_track: Nightly reconciliation divergence - target <0.1% vs raw sums
Console API P95 latency - target <300ms for top-10k routes
Storage cost for Chronicle pipeline - keep <5% of overall infra econ spend initially
Number of reconciliation corrections (absolute) per day - trending down after fixes
